chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-02.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-02.body: Differentiate $\cos(\sin(\cos x))$: $-\sin(\sin\cos x)\cdot\cos(\cos x)\cdot(-\sin x)$, which is the integrand.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-03.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-03.body: By parts with $u=\operatorname{arcsec}\sqrt x$, $dv=dx$: $\frac{d}{dx}\operatorname{arcsec}\sqrt x=\frac1{2x\sqrt{x-1}}$, so $\int=x\operatorname{arcsec}\sqrt x-\int\frac{dx}{2\sqrt{x-1}}=x\operatorname{arcsec}\sqrt x-\sqrt{x-1}+C$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-04.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-04.body: For $0\le x\le1$: $|1-x|=1-x$, then $|1-(1-x)|=x$, then $|1-x|=1-x$. So the integral is $\int_0^1(1-x)dx=\frac12$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-06.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-06.body: $\frac{d}{dx}(\sec x\ln x)=\sec x\tan x\ln x+\frac{\sec x}x$, so the integral is $\big[\sec x\ln x\big]_1^{\pi/3}=2\ln\frac\pi3-0$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-08.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-08.body: Let $u=x-3\sqrt x$, $du=\frac{2\sqrt x-3}{2\sqrt x}dx$. Since $2x-9\sqrt x+9=(2\sqrt x-3)(\sqrt x-3)$, the integrand times $dx$ is $\frac{2\sqrt x(\sqrt x-3)}{u^{1/3}}du=2u^{2/3}du$, giving $\frac65u^{5/3}+C$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-11.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-11.body: $\sin(\arccos x)=\sqrt{1-x^2}$ for $-1\le x\le1$, and $\int\sqrt{1-x^2}dx=\frac12(x\sqrt{1-x^2}+\arcsin x)+C$ (equivalently $\frac12x\sqrt{1-x^2}-\frac12\arccos x+C$).

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-14.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-14.body: Let $u=\sqrt{x^{2025}-1}$, so $x^{2025}=u^2+1$ and $2025\frac{dx}x=\frac{2u\,du}{u^2+1}$. The integral becomes $\int\frac{2}{2025(u^2+1)}du=\frac2{2025}\arctan u+C$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-15.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-15.body: $\frac{d}{dx}(xe^x\sin x)=e^x\sin x+xe^x(\sin x+\cos x)$, so $\int xe^x(\sin x+\cos x)dx=xe^x\sin x-\int e^x\sin x\,dx=xe^x\sin x-\frac{e^x(\sin x-\cos x)}2+C$. (Over $[0,1]$ this equals $\frac{e(\sin1+\cos1)-1}2$, the value shown on the official answer slide.)

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-16.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-16.body: The curves $y=(1-x^{25})^{1/20}$ and $y=(1-x^{20})^{1/25}$ are inverse functions of each other on $[0,1]$ ($y^{20}+x^{25}=1\iff x^{25}+y^{20}=1$), so each integral equals the area of the same region $\{x^{25}+y^{20}\le1\}$ in the first quadrant. The difference is $0$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-19.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-19.body: $\cot x-\tan x=2\cot2x$ and $\cos4x+1=2\cos^22x$, so the integrand is $\cos2x\sin2x=\frac12\sin4x$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-20.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-20.body: $\frac1{\sin^3x\cos^2x}=\frac{\sin^2x+\cos^2x}{\sin^3x\cos^2x}=\frac1{\sin x\cos^2x}+\frac1{\sin^3x}$, and $\frac1{\sin x\cos^2x}=\frac{\sin x}{\cos^2x}+\frac1{\sin x}$. Use $\int\frac{\sin x}{\cos^2x}dx=\sec x$, $\int\csc x\,dx=\ln|\tan\frac x2|$ and $\int\csc^3x\,dx=-\frac12\csc x\cot x+\frac12\ln|\tan\frac x2|$. (Differentiating the result confirms it.)

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-21.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-21.body: $1+\cos x=2\cos^2\frac x2$ and $\sin x=2\sin\frac x2\cos\frac x2$, so the integrand is $\frac{x}{2}\sec^2\frac x2+\tan\frac x2=\frac d{dx}\left(x\tan\frac x2\right)$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-23.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-23.body: $1-\sin x=2\sin^2\left(\frac\pi4-\frac x2\right)$ and $1+\sin x=2\cos^2\left(\frac\pi4-\frac x2\right)$, so the square root is $\left|\tan\left(\frac\pi4-\frac x2\right)\right|$. For $-\frac\pi2\le x\le\frac\pi2$ the angle $\frac\pi4-\frac x2$ lies in $[0,\frac\pi2]$, so the integrand equals $\frac\pi4-\frac x2$ and the integral is $\frac{\pi x}4-\frac{x^2}4+C$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-25.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-25.body: The exponent $g(x)=x^{2025}\cos x$ is odd, so $\frac1{1+e^{g(x)}}+\frac1{1+e^{g(-x)}}=\frac1{1+e^g}+\frac1{1+e^{-g}}=1$. Hence the integral $I$ satisfies $2I=\int e^{-x^2}dx=\sqrt\pi$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-26.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-26.body: Under $x\mapsto\frac\pi2-x$ the denominator $2025-x^2+\frac{\pi x}2$ is unchanged (check: $-(\frac\pi2-x)^2+\frac\pi2(\frac\pi2-x)=-x^2+\frac{\pi x}2$) while $\cos x-\sin x$ changes sign. So $I=-I$, $I=0$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-27.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-27.body: $\frac1{1+e^{s}}+\frac1{1+e^{-s}}=1$, and $\sin(x+\pi)=-\sin x$, so on each period $[0,2\pi]$ the integral is $\int_0^\pi\left(\frac1{1+e^{\sin x}}+\frac1{1+e^{-\sin x}}\right)dx=\pi$. There are $1013$ periods: $1013\pi$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-28.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-28.body: $\frac{1-\cos x}{1+\cos x}=\tan^2\frac x2$, so the integrand is $\tan^{3/5}\frac x2\cdot\frac1{1+\cos x}=\frac12\tan^{3/5}\frac x2\sec^2\frac x2$. With $u=\tan\frac x2$, $du=\frac12\sec^2\frac x2dx$: $\int u^{3/5}du=\frac58u^{8/5}$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-29.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-29.body: $\ln\frac{\pi-x}{\pi+x}$ is odd, so $\ln(\cdot)\cos x$ integrates to $0$. Then $\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}x^2\cos x\,dx=\big[x^2\sin x+2x\cos x-2\sin x\big]_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}=2\left(\frac{\pi^2}4-2\right)=\frac{\pi^2}2-4$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-30.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-30.body: Let $t=\tan x$, $dx=\frac{dt}{1+t^2}$, $\cos^2x=\frac1{1+t^2}$: $\int\frac{dt}{1+2025(1+t^2)}=\int\frac{dt}{2026+2025t^2}=\frac1{\sqrt{2026\cdot2025}}\arctan\left(\sqrt{\tfrac{2025}{2026}}\,t\right)$. (On each interval between poles; adding $\frac{k\pi}{45\sqrt{2026}}$ on the $k$-th interval makes it continuous.)

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-31.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-31.body: $\cos2x-\cos^2x=-\sin^2x$, so the integrand is $\frac{2\sin x\cos x-\sin^2x}{-\sin^2x}=1-2\cot x$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-36.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-36.body: Divide numerator and denominator by $\cos^4x$ and put $t=\tan x$: $\int\frac{(1+t^2)\,dt}{t^4+1}=\int\frac{(1+1/t^2)dt}{t^2+1/t^2}$. With $w=t-\frac1t$, $dw=(1+\frac1{t^2})dt$, $t^2+\frac1{t^2}=w^2+2$: $\frac1{\sqrt2}\arctan\frac w{\sqrt2}$. Since $\arctan a+\arctan b=\arctan\frac{a+b}{1-ab}$ (up to $\pi$), $\arctan(\sqrt2t+1)+\arctan(\sqrt2t-1)=\frac\pi2+\arctan\frac{t^2-1}{\sqrt2t}$ for $t>0$, so the stated form differs from $\frac1{\sqrt2}\arctan\frac w{\sqrt2}$ only by a constant on each interval (also checked numerically).

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-37.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-37.body: By parts twice: $\int x\ln^2x\,dx=\frac{x^2}2\ln^2x-\int x\ln x\,dx=\frac{x^2}2\ln^2x-\frac{x^2}2\ln x+\frac{x^2}4$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-40.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-40.body: With $u=\sin x-\cos x$, $du=(\cos x+\sin x)dx$ and $\sin2x=1-u^2$: $\int\frac{du}{\sqrt{1-u^2}}=\arcsin u$. At $x=\frac\pi3$: $u=\frac{\sqrt3-1}2$; at $x=\frac\pi6$: $u=-\frac{\sqrt3-1}2$. Result $2\arcsin\frac{\sqrt3-1}2\approx0.7495$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-41.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-41.body: Let $u=e^x$: $-\int\sqrt{4u^2-9}\,du$. The standard result $\int\sqrt{4u^2-9}\,du=\frac u2\sqrt{4u^2-9}-\frac94\ln\left(2u+\sqrt{4u^2-9}\right)+C$ (by parts or $2u=3\cosh\theta$) gives the stated antiderivative.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-42.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-42.body: Let $u=\sqrt[3]x$, $dx=3u^2du$: $\int\frac{3u^3}{1+u^3}du=3u-3\int\frac{du}{1+u^3}$, and $\frac1{1+u^3}=\frac13\left(\frac1{u+1}-\frac{u-2}{u^2-u+1}\right)$ gives the logarithms and arctangent.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-43.title: Differentiate under the integral sign
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-43.body: Let $I(a)=\int_0^\infty\frac{\sin(ax)}xe^{-x^2}dx$, $I(0)=0$. Then $I'(a)=\int_0^\infty\cos(ax)e^{-x^2}dx=\frac{\sqrt\pi}2e^{-a^2/4}$, so $I(a)=\frac\pi2\operatorname{erf}\frac a2$. The required integral is $I(\sqrt3)-I(1/\sqrt3)=\frac\pi2\left(\operatorname{erf}\frac{\sqrt3}2-\operatorname{erf}\frac{1}{2\sqrt3}\right)\approx0.72637$ (confirmed by numerical integration).

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-45.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-45.body: Since $\tan(\arctan x+\arctan(1-x))=\frac{1}{1-x(1-x)}=\frac1{x^2-x+1}$, we have $\arctan\frac1{x^2-x+1}=\arctan x+\arctan(1-x)$, hence $\arctan(x^2-x+1)=\frac\pi2-\arctan x-\arctan(1-x)$. Integrating over $[0,1]$ (the two arctan terms have equal integrals): $\frac\pi2-2\int_0^1\arctan x\,dx=\frac\pi2-2\left(\frac\pi4-\frac{\ln2}2\right)=\ln2$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-46.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-46.body: Let $J(a)=\int_0^\infty e^{-x^2}\cos(ax)dx$. Differentiating and integrating by parts: $J'(a)=-\int_0^\infty xe^{-x^2}\sin(ax)dx=-\frac a2J(a)$, so $J(a)=J(0)e^{-a^2/4}=\frac{\sqrt\pi}2e^{-a^2/4}$. At $a=2$: $\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2e}$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-48.title: Solution
chmmc-cmm-2025-bee-final-48.body: $2x^2(1-\cos\theta)=4x^2\sin^2\frac\theta2$, so each factor is $2|x|\sin\frac{\pi k}n$. Using $\prod_{k=1}^{n-1}2\sin\frac{\pi k}n=n$, the product is $n|x|^{n-1}$, whose antiderivative is $x|x|^{n-1}$.
